title: evidence-hunting-playbook
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal playbook for hunting down SOC 2 evidence and working around gaps when doing early collection. Not an official runbook — rough notes for teammates.

Scope / assumptions:
- Focus = controls that need artifacts (logs, configs, runbooks, screenshots, invoices).
- We are prepping for a readiness review (internal) before engaging an auditor.
- Prioritize controls that auditors usually hit hard: logical access, change control, backup, monitoring/alerts.

High-level approach:
1) Identify control owner (if unknown, flag in tracker).
2) Pull candidate evidence from system(s) and snapshot with date-stamped filename.
3) If evidence missing, create interim compensating evidence (ticket, owner attestation, screenshot of plan).
4) Log every evidence item in tracker with location + capture method.

Quick search checklist (CLI / grep ideas):
- GCP logs: use date windows, search for "iam.policy" or "gcloud projects get-iam-policy" entries.
- GitHub: repo:infra "approved-by" OR "deploy: v" in PR titles.
- S3/GCS: ls -l --recursive | grep -E "backup|snapshot|dbdump"
- Vault: list secret engines -> map to service accounts and owners.
- Slack: search in #security and #on-call for "incident" "pager" (use workspace export where available).

Evidence locations (common):
- infra repo: ops runbooks, IaC templates (Terraform state), PR history for change control.
- observability: Grafana dashboards export + alert history.
- cloud storage: backup snapshots, DB export folder names (include retention metadata).
- billing: invoices for third-party backups, SaaS contracts (retention, encryption).
- identity providers: Okta admin audit logs, service account listing.

Control -> candidate evidence mapping (quick pass):
- Logical access reviews: Okta org report (users + groups), monthly review notes (Confluence). If missing: owner attestation + current csv export.
- Provisioning/deprovisioning: PRs that create IAM bindings, GCP audit logs showing role creation. If missing: runbook + ticket for outstanding deprovs.
- Change approval: GitHub PRs with approvals + merge timestamps, JIRA ticket link. If gap: capture release notes and an email thread approving the change.
- Backups: GCS bucket manifest + retention policy, snapshot timestamps. If missing: scheduled backup job config screenshot + ticket to enable.
- Monitoring/alerts: PagerDuty escalation policy + alert rule exports, slack alert channel logs. If missing: demonstration alert configured in staging + screenshot.

Evidence capture conventions (my rules):
- Filenames: YYYYMMDD_control_shortname_owner_method (e.g., 20260301_logicalaccess_okta_export_liam.csv).
- Store raw + derived: raw export kept (raw-YYYYMMDD-...), derived summary (summary-...).
- Annotate: one-line header inside file with what it proves and time window.

Temporary compensating evidence (examples):
- Attestation template (signed email from owner): "I confirm access list for X reviewed on DATE".
- Ticket proof: create ticket with checklist and link to steps we will take. Use JIRA-SEC tag.
- Screenshot + timestamped terminal cmd demonstrating a config exists when we cannot export a machine-readable report.

Open questions / flags to resolve:
- Which controls exactly require vendor contracts for hosted inference components? (list out in Confluence)
- Do we have a single source-of-truth for backup retention policy? I think billing/legal have SLA documents.
- Need standardized export scripts for Okta / GCP / GitHub so reviewers don't receive ad-hoc csvs.

Short-term action items (this week):
- [ ] Run Okta export and mark owners for any accounts with admin roles (assign to Maya).
- [ ] Get infra repo branch protection proof + list of approvers (Ellie).
- [ ] Snapshot backup manifests for DB clusters and put into evidence-bucket (Liam).
- [ ] Draft owner-attestation template and circulate for quick signatures.

Audit-day quick checklist (one-pagers):
- Bring: 1) evidence index spreadsheet, 2) raw exports, 3) owner attestation emails, 4) contact list for control owners.\- Have Slack channel ready: #audit-quick if auditor has quick questions.

Templates / snippets (to copy-paste):
- Attestation email: "I, [NAME], attest that I am the owner of [CONTROL], and on [DATE] I have reviewed the attached artifact which demonstrates compliance for the period [START-END]."
- Evidence index row example: "control_id, filename, location, owner, capture_method, notes"

Evidence index (minimal columns):
- control_id
- control_short_description
- filename_or_url
- owner
- capture_date
- method (export/screenshot/attestation)
- status (collected/missing/compensating)

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Auditors trust reproducible exports more than screenshots. When in doubt, invest time in a csv export.
- If a control has episodic evidence (e.g., monthly review), capture multiple months but highlight the sample month used for testing.
- Keep a running document of any compensating controls used and why — auditors ask about permanence after the fact.
- Timebox evidence hunting per control to 2 hours max on first pass then escalate.

End-of-day log (example):
- 2026-03-01: ran Okta export (raw-20260301-okta.csv), flagged 3 orphaned service accounts (JIRA-SEC-412).
- 2026-03-02: captured DB snapshot manifest (raw-20260302-db-manifest.json), uploaded to evidence-bucket (evidence/20260302/).

Questions for Maya / Ellie (ping during pairing):
- Maya: can you run the weekly access review script and drop CSV in evidence/tmp?
- Ellie: can you export the repo branch protection config and list of CODEOWNERS?

If stuck: fallback to owner attestation + ticket that outlines remediation timeline. Make sure ticket is linked to evidence index.

——
Personal note: keep this informal and editable. When we have a stable checklist, move to Confluence and create automation for exports.
